Resolves #20270

Guards `Neo.grid.header.Button#afterSetResizable` (`src/grid/header/Button.mjs:239-258`) so its asynchronous `import('./plugin/Resizable.mjs').then(...)` callback checks `!me.isDestroyed && !me.isDestroying && me.resizable && !me.getPlugin('plugin-grid-header-resizable')` before mutating `me.plugins`, matching the sibling lazy-import guards in `ensureHeaderFilterProjection()` (`src/grid/header/Button.mjs:300`) and `afterSetColumnMenu()` (`src/grid/header/Button.mjs:322`). Promoted from `@neo-opus-vega`'s `defect-note` (`MESSAGE:4fc05074-0c0b-46b9-89d7-2e199044bb91`).

Evidence: L2 (Playwright unit spec under `test/playwright/playwright.config.unit.mjs`) → L2 required (AC-1..AC-3). Residual: none.

Micro-review eligible: mechanical-guard — applies the exact `!me.isDestroyed && !me.isDestroying` lazy-import guard already used by `ensureHeaderFilterProjection` and `afterSetColumnMenu` in `src/grid/header/Button.mjs`.

| AC-1 | `src/grid/header/Button.mjs:244` (`!me.isDestroyed && !me.isDestroying && me.resizable && !me.getPlugin('plugin-grid-header-resizable')`) |

# PR Micro-Review

**Class:** mechanical — this is the lazy-import guard the class's two siblings already use, applied at the third call site. It teaches no new concept.

**Verdict:** Approved

**Glance:** The claim is that `afterSetResizable`'s lazy `Resizable` import wrote `plugins` onto a header button that had already been destroyed. At `462675b598`, the callback now checks `!me.isDestroyed && !me.isDestroying && me.resizable && !me.getPlugin('plugin-grid-header-resizable')`, exactly like `ensureHeaderFilterProjection()` and `afterSetColumnMenu()`. That also covers a `resizable: false` that arrives before the import resolves, and a second import racing the first.

I ran one falsifier. The new arm passes at head. With only `src/grid/header/Button.mjs` reverted to the merge-base, it fails on the captured "'plugins' was set after destroy()" warning, so it guards the defect rather than the code's shape. (`btn.plugins` stays `null` either way, because the setter ignores the write; the warning assertion is the one that discriminates.) The diff touches only the prescribed site and its spec. CI is green at head: 52 passed, 1 skipped.
